raw_response:
I farm like my mother-in-law taught me. 4.1 mu is not much, so I count every yuan. I do wheat in winter, then maize right after in summer — same as everyone in our village.

For wheat planting, I buy one bag of compound fertilizer per mu from the dealer — the 15-15-15 kind, 40 kg bag. That is my base. Then in spring when wheat stands up, I broadcast half a bag of urea per mu before watering. If the color looks pale I add a little more, but usually that is enough. I buy seed from the same shop as my neighbor Zhang — she got good wheat last year so I use what she uses, improved seed, not the old kind. I water wheat maybe three times — once before winter, once at green-up, once when grain is filling. If rain comes I skip one. I spray twice, one for weeds after winter, one for aphids and the rust when I see it on leaves.

For summer maize I plant right after wheat harvest, no ploughing, just rotary — my husband rents the machine from the village. I put one bag compound at sowing, then one topdressing of urea, maybe 15 kg per mu when the maize is knee-high. Maize drinks a lot so I water two times if no rain. I spray once for borer. Hybrid seed, the dealer recommends one and everybody buys it.

Last year wheat gave me about 500 jin per mu, maize a bit more. I hope for the same. I would rather put a little extra fertilizer than have a thin crop — a bad harvest is too painful.
